about.title: Newark Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Newark's public-record data shows 105 injury collisions and 138 people hurt in the most recent reporting year, with Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. showing up as a common crash window. Corridors like Cedar Boulevard, Thornton Avenue, Cherry Street, and Newark Boulevard carry a lot of daily traffic, and that volume translates into real people dealing with real injuries and insurance headaches. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured drivers, passengers, cyclists, and pedestrians in Newark with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened. California gives you a limited window to act, and the sooner evidence gets preserved (skid marks, dashcam footage, witness contacts), the stronger a claim tends to be. There's no obligation and no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Talk to the Other Driver's Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window shrinks dramatically — sometimes to six months — if a government entity (like a city road crew or public bus) was involved. Waiting to sort out fault can cost you the ability to file at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Case
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash — your compensation is just reduced by your share of fault. An independent attorney can help make sure the insurer doesn't unfairly inflate your percentage of blame.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Backfire
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement right after a crash, before you know the full extent of your injuries. California law doesn't require you to give one, and anything you say can later be used to minimize your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Newark car accident?
items.answer: In California, you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months, if a government vehicle or agency was involved, such as an AC Transit bus or a city maintenance truck. It's worth getting a claim reviewed early so you don't lose the option to pursue one.

items.question: Does it matter if the crash happened on a busy road like Cedar Boulevard or Thornton Avenue?
items.answer: Where a crash happens doesn't change your legal rights, but heavier traffic corridors can mean more witnesses, more traffic camera coverage, and more insurance companies involved if multiple vehicles are hit. An attorney can help track down that evidence before it disappears.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, so being partially responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation — it just reduces the amount by your percentage of fault. Insurers sometimes try to shift more blame onto injured people than is fair, which is one reason having independent representation matters.
